what_happened: Found that task 421 (retarget_distill_meta_as_evidence_consumer) already exists and is explicitly scoped as the deliberate batched consumer this task's dispatch describes, confirming the dispatch's own framing without needing to invent or verify that claim independently. Also found an exact existing schema precedent (events.jsonl's push_grant_issued/push_grant_consumed rows, category:milestone, rich structured detail object) for recording a non-deviation/non-blocker classification-shaped record in events.jsonl, which strongly informed the recommended storage design (append classification records to events.jsonl via events-append.sh rather than issues.jsonl, since issues.jsonl re-entry would create a self-referential re-classification loop under the stage's own filter predicate).

Research report's consumer table omitted five files that reference the conclusion stage or its channels (commands/orchestrate.md, skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, scripts/issue-record.sh, context/formats/issue-log.md, context/contracts/batch-gate-stage.md). A planning-time grep sweep checked all five and confirmed none needs an edit, but the confirmation had to be redone rather than inherited. The report also asserted task 421 'depends on nothing listed against 402'; live state.json shows its dependencies are [312, 402]. Neither changes the plan; both are recorded in the plan's Research Integration section so the implementer does not re-derive them.

Running suite_selection_select over each phase's Files to modify paths before writing the Tier Justification lines produced exact, verbatim-matching covering-suite claims in under a minute, including the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel for the four pure-markdown consumer files. This removed all guesswork from the tier declarations and directly surfaced that conclusion-stage.md's covering suite IS test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh -- which is why the contract rewrite and its test rewrite had to be one phase rather than two.

Phase 2's own named verification (verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow --only-gate 3,4) reported core FAIL, but the sole cause is a pre-existing, unrelated deploy-drift advisory (agent-system/extensions/books/scripts/books-observe.sh not yet deployed to .claude/scripts/) -- nothing this phase touched. Gate 4 (task-reference lint) passed cleanly. Deferred to Phase 3's deploy-headless.sh, which redeploys the whole tree and will resolve the drift.

deploy-headless.sh's verify step reports RESULT=landed_verify_red on two gates, neither caused by this task: (1) gate10 (validate-state.sh --deep) consistently exceeds its own 60s per-gate timeout inside the pipeline's concurrent gate runner, though the same check run standalone (outside that timeout wrapper) completes in ~50s and surfaces exactly one pre-existing content finding, Check 12: next_project_number (607) collides with an in-use project_number -- independently owned by task_number_allocation_staleness_undetected and confirmed byte-identical to this task's pre-dispatch baseline via git show (3927bddbd:specs/state.json shows 607, current specs/state.json shows 607). (2) gate20 (measure-eager-context.sh) reports eager-load total 71712B over baseline 70400B, attributable solely to commands/orchestrate.md and skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, neither touched by this task; this exact figure is already documented as a pre-existing cross-task condition in specs/TODO.md, specs/state.json (task 391's channel-c proposal), and specs/397_lean_research_compile_verify_recommendation's phase-4 handoff. All of this task's own verification criteria (conclusion-stage.md net line count -23 negative, deployed-copy test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh 14/14 passing including cases g/i/j/k, orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh and events-schema.json byte-identical/untouched, next_project_number unchanged) are independently confirmed green.
